title: Appendix B — Equation list: CPAT code names
text:
B.2 Executive summary: core equations
One year of the model, in the order of the calculation chain (spec section 4.3): policies and prices (computed for all years before the year loop), then fuel use, power, revenues, emissions and GDP, then distribution in its analysis year.

B.2.1 M0 Header: macro series
The macro series of the country and the header rows that read them (Excel-AI sheet Inputs_macro, legacy Mitigation rows 417-467). Quantity-free: computed for all years before the year loop.
M0.1 Macro series past the last data year
\[
\mathtt{gdp\_usd}_t = \begin{cases} \mathtt{ngdp}_t / \mathtt{xr}_t \cdot \mathtt{deflidx}_t & t < \mathtt{BaseYr} \\ \mathtt{gdp\_usd}_{t-1}\,(1 + \mathtt{gdp\_growth}_t) & t \ge \mathtt{BaseYr} \end{cases}, \qquad \mathtt{gdp\_lcu}_t = \mathtt{ngdp\_r}_t
\]
Over macro years 2018-2045; series \(x\): US deflator and CPI, real GDP growth, real and nominal GDP, exchange rate, population. Excel-AI notation. Extensions: US deflator linear (\(2x_{t-1} - x_{t-2}\)); US CPI, exchange rate flat; real GDP grown with \(g\); nominal GDP with its last growth rate, held from the last data year of nominal GDP (Excel-AI: the growth of the last data year is the year before’s); population with its last growth factor. The exchange rate of a euro country is the euro area’s (WEO G163). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_macro (build_inputs_macro).
M0.2 Inflation and deflator indices, real GDP, exchange rate
\[
\mathtt{infl}_t = \mathtt{CPIRes} / \mathtt{pcpi}_t, \qquad \mathtt{defl}_t = \mathtt{DeflRes} / \mathtt{ngdp\_d}_t, \qquad \mathtt{xr}_t = \mathtt{gdp.lcu}_t / \mathtt{gdp.usd}_t
\]
\(R\) is the results year (MTInputs ResultsYear, read from the baseline column). \(\nu_t\) converts nominal domestic prices and policy inputs to real, \(\delta_t\) international prices. Excel-AI notation. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation rows 8-13 (section 0).


B.2.2 M1 Policies
Every policy is a path from a start year to a target year, set per scenario.
M1.1 Policy path (linear from a start to a target level)
\[
\mathtt{path}(t;\ \mathtt{start\_year},\ \mathtt{target\_year},\ \mathtt{start\_level},\ \mathtt{target\_level})
\]
Excel-AI notation (the methodology describes the paths in words). Held flat after \(T_1\) unless the input says the path continues. Source: Excel-AI: Equations.md section 0 (Λ, Λ̄).
M1.2 National carbon tax per tonne
\[
\mathtt{cptraj}_t = \mathtt{path}(t;\ \mathtt{CPIntro},\ \mathtt{CPOutro},\ \mathtt{CPLevelStart},\ \mathtt{CPLevelTarget})\cdot \mathtt{infl}_t
\]
\(\nu_t\) is the CPI index (US CPI of the results year over year \(t\)) if the inputs are nominal, else 1 (Excel-AI notation). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Prices > Notation (\(NCT\)); Excel-AI: E1.
M1.3 New carbon tax and ETS cost by sector
\[
\mathtt{ctr}_{s,t} = \mathtt{cptraj}_t\,\mathtt{ctcov}_{s}\,(1 - \mathtt{etsc}_{s,t}), \qquad \mathtt{etr}_{s,t} = \mathtt{ets.pe}_t\,\mathtt{etsc}_{s,t}\,(1 - \mathtt{obr}_{s,t})
\]
Over sectors \(s\) (power and the 16 subsectors). \(\kappa_s\) new-ETS coverage, \(\omega_s\) share allocated free (output-based), \(\tilde{p}^E\) the tax-equivalent ETS price (Excel-AI notation; methodology \(NETSP\) is the national ETS price). Where the new tax complements an existing ETS, \(\varphi_{NCT,s}\) is one minus the existing ETS coverage. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Prices > Notation (\(NCT\), \(NETSP\), \(\varphi_{NCT/ETS}\)); Excel-AI: E5, E6, E13-E15.
M1.4 Shadow price of non-pricing policies by sector
\[
\mathtt{shpx}_{s,t} = \mathtt{fb}_{g(s),t}\,\mathtt{ssc}_{s} + \mathtt{reg}_{s,t} + \mathtt{ets.pe}_t\,\mathtt{etsc}_{s,t}\,\mathtt{obr}_{s,t}, \qquad \mathtt{reg}_{s,t} = \mathtt{cp.shd}_t\,\mathtt{regadj}\,\mathtt{regc}_{s}
\]
Over sectors \(s\); \(g(s)\) is the sector group of \(s\). Excel-AI notation: \(b_g\) feebate rate of the feebate sector, \(a\) share of the feebate on the efficiency margin (SPPEffAdjFeebates where the feebate covers \(s\)). \(reg\): under a main scenario with shadow pricing (MTInputs ScenarioSelected; table of main scenarios), the shadow carbon price (\(\Lambda\) less the explicit price) times the efficiency adjustment of the scenario, in the sectors it covers. The shadow price acts on the efficiency margin only (M3.1); it raises no revenue. Source: Excel-AI: E3, E16.
M1.5 Fuel price reform path
\[
\mathtt{fpr}_{c,t},\quad \mathtt{fprj}_c = \frac{\mathtt{fpr.f}_c - \mathtt{fpr.s}_c}{\mathtt{FprOutro} - \mathtt{FprIntro}},\quad \mathtt{fprk}_c = \left(\frac{\mathtt{fpr.f}_c}{\mathtt{fpr.s}_c}\right)^{1/(T_1 - T_0)} - 1,\quad \mathtt{fprp}_c = \mathtt{fpr.s}_c + \mathtt{fprj}_c\,\max(T_1 - T_0 - 1, 0)
\]
Over price fuels \(c\) (coal and gas by power, residential, industry; electricity residential and industry; oil products and biomass). Excel-AI notation. The path after the target year follows ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro: Linear* continues the line, Percentage grows at the rate \(k\) from \(p\), otherwise held at \(x_1\). Where the start is zero the rate divides by \(x_0 + j\). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (fprj, fprk, fprp, fpra, fpr).
M1.6 Social cost of carbon
\[
\mathtt{scc}_{nat,t},\ \mathtt{scc}_{glo,t} \in \{\mathtt{scc}_{tgt,t},\ \mathtt{scc}_{rkn|rkg,t},\ \mathtt{scc}_{man,t},\ \mathtt{scc}_{epa,t}\}
\]
Excel-AI notation. Target-consistent price, Ricke et al. (2018) national or global (sheet SCC, by discount rate and elasticity), manual path, US EPA; the national and global SCC are chosen by NSCCSource and GSCCSource (read from the baseline column). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (scc).
M1.7 Phase-out factor of subsidies and price controls
\[
\mathtt{pof}_{k,t};\quad \mathtt{csf}_{c,t} = 1 - \mathtt{csi}_c\,(1 - \mathtt{pof}_{cs,t}),\quad \mathtt{pcf}_{c,t} = 1 - \mathtt{pci}_c\,(1 - \mathtt{pof}_{pc,t}),\quad \mathtt{psf}_{f,t} = 1 - \mathtt{psi}_f\,(1 - \mathtt{pof}_{ps,t})
\]
Over phase-outs \(k\): producer subsidies, consumer subsidies, price controls; price fuels \(c\) or producer fuels \(f\). Excel-AI notation. The baseline uses the baseline switch, period and share; a policy scenario its own switch and period and the larger of the two shares. Price controls are on only where the policy switch is on (and, in the baseline, the baseline switch too); they use the consumer-subsidy shares (Excel-AI issue I48). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (po.on, po.n, po.sh, pof, csf, pcf, psf).
M1.8 Methane fee
\[
\mathtt{mfee}_t = \mathtt{mfee.p}_t\,\mathbb{1}[o > 1] + \mathtt{cptraj}_t\,\mathbb{1}[\mathtt{CTforMethane}]
\]
Excel-AI notation. The fee path continues linearly after its target year. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (mfee.p, mfee).


B.2.3 M2 Energy prices
Prices before policies by sector group \(g\) and fuel \(f\) (the methodology’s price sectors), then new policies and the after-tax price by sector \(s\) and fuel \(f\). All quantity-free: computed for all years before the year loop.
M2.1 Supply price (fixed part plus a floating part that follows the international price)
\[
\mathtt{sp}_{t} = \mathtt{spf} + (\mathtt{sp}_{t-1} - \mathtt{spf} - \mathtt{ps}_{t-1})\,\frac{\mathtt{gpi}_t}{\mathtt{gpi}_{t-1}} + \mathtt{ps}_t
\]
Over sector groups \(g\), fuels \(f\); projection years \(t > L\) (last historical price year). The methodology writes \(sp = fixsp + fltsp + ps\) with \(fltsp_t = fltsp_{t-1}\,gp_t/gp_{t-1}\). \(gp\) is the international price of the price fuel’s commodity (oil, coal, the country’s gas market; biomass flat), real, times the High / Low factor after \(L\); \(ps\) the producer subsidy per unit (A2.5). Historical years: data (A2.4). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C > Calculations (supply price, floating portion); Excel-AI: E19, E20.
M2.2 Excise and other taxes, floating with the pass-through
\[
\mathtt{txf}_t = \mathtt{txf}_{t-1} - (\mathtt{sp}_t - \mathtt{sp}_{t-1})\,(1 - \mathtt{pcc})
\]
Over sector groups \(g\), fuels \(f\). \(pcc\) is the price-control (pass-through) coefficient: 1 for a liberalised market, 0 for fixed prices. A positive tax does not fall below its last historical level (appendix A2). Here \(txo\) holds existing taxes and subsidies only; the methodology’s \(txo\) also includes the carbon prices, which Excel-AI keeps apart (M2.5). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C > Calculations (\(flts\), \(pcc\)); Excel-AI: E21-E23.
M2.3 VAT and retail price before new policies
\[
\mathtt{vat}_t = (\mathtt{sp}_t + \mathtt{txo}_t)\,\mathtt{vr}, \qquad \mathtt{pbc}_t = (\mathtt{sp}_t + \mathtt{txo}_t)(1 + \mathtt{vr})
\]
Over sector groups \(g\), fuels \(f\). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C > Calculations (VAT, retail price); Excel-AI: E24, E25.
M2.4 New carbon price, ETS cost and excise per unit of energy
\[
\mathtt{ctxnew}_{s,f} = \mathtt{ctr}_s\,\mathtt{ef}_{s,f}\,\mathtt{ctcov}_f\,\mathtt{exf}_{s,f}, \quad \mathtt{ets}_{s,f} = \mathtt{etr}_s\,\mathtt{ef}_{s,f}\,\mathtt{exf}_{s,f}, \quad \mathtt{ntx}_{s,f} = \frac{\mathtt{fpr}_{g,f}}{\mathtt{gju}^{\dagger}_{g,f}}\,\mathtt{exf}_{s,f}
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\); \(g\) is the price sector of \((s,f)\). \(ef\) the calibrated CO2 emission factor (M7.1), \(x\) the exemption factor (0 for an exempt fuel), \(F^x\) the fuel-price reform path (M1.1) in price units and \(u\) GJ per price unit (Excel-AI notation for \(x\), \(F^x\), \(u\)). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C > Calculations (\(ncp = nct + netsp\), \(nexc\)); Excel-AI: E26-E29.
M2.5 After-tax price
\[
\mathtt{atp}_{s,f} = \max\!\big(\mathtt{rpb}_{g,f} + (\mathtt{ctxnew}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ets}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ntx}_{s,f} + \mathtt{xcpd}_{s,f})\,(1 + \mathtt{vatr}^{\dagger}_{g,f}),\ \mathtt{PriceFloor}\big)
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\). \(\Delta xcp\) is the change in existing carbon pricing against the price data, which already contain it (appendix A2). \(\underline{p}\) is the price floor (0.01). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C > Calculations (retail price); Excel-AI: E30, E31.
M2.6 Shadow price per unit of energy
\[
\mathtt{shp}_{s,f} = \mathtt{shpx}_{s}\,\mathtt{ef}_{s,f}
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\). Excel-AI notation (the methodology names the shadow price in words only). Source: Excel-AI: E32.


B.2.4 M3 Fuel use
The core behavioural equation of CPAT (switchable slot fuel demand, spec section 7).
M3.1 Fuel use, constant-elasticity form
\[
\frac{\mathtt{enel}_{s,f,t}}{\mathtt{enel}_{s,f,t-1}} = \left(\frac{1}{1 + \mathtt{eff\_imp}_{s,f} + \mathtt{addeff}^{\dagger}_{s,t}}\right)^{1 + \mathtt{el\_dem}} \mathtt{shock}_t\,(1 + \mathtt{gdp.pos.pct}_t)^{\mathtt{el\_inc}\cdot\mathtt{incf}_t} \left(\frac{\mathtt{atp}_{s,f,t}}{\mathtt{atp}_{s,f,t-1}}\right)^{\mathtt{el\_dem}} \left(\frac{\mathtt{atp}_{s,f,t} + \mathtt{shp}_{s,f,t}}{\mathtt{atp}_{s,f,t-1} + \mathtt{shp}_{s,f,t-1}}\right)^{\mathtt{el\_eff}\,(1 + \mathtt{el\_dem})}
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\); the elasticities \(\epsilon_Y, \epsilon_U, \epsilon_F\) vary by country, sector and fuel. As the methodology, with three Excel-AI additions: the shadow price enters the efficiency term only; \(\alpha^{+}_{s}\) is the additional policy-induced efficiency gain of the sector’s group (Excel-AI notation); \(inc_t\) adjusts the income elasticity to the income level (Excel-AI notation). \(\Psi_t\) is the demand shock (methodology: Covid adjustment; in Excel-AI the 2023-2024 shock, switch on). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Fuel Consumption Dynamics; Excel-AI: E69 (LAMBDAs FUELUSE, AEEIFACTOR).
M3.2 Fuel use used by the rest of the model
\[
\mathtt{ener}_{s,f} = \begin{cases} \mathtt{trfc}^{\dagger}_{f} & s = \mathtt{rod},\ \mathtt{TrModel} = \text{Engineer} \\ \mathtt{enel}_{s,f} + \mathtt{lkc}_{s,f} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\). \(F^e\) is M3.1, \(F^T\) the road engineer model (M5), \(Lk\) residential leakage to biomass (appendix A3, off by default). Excel-AI notation for the superscripts. Source: Excel-AI: E69, ROADSWITCH, section 6b.
M3.3 Energy use totals and change against the baseline
\[
\mathtt{ener}_{S,all}, \ \mathtt{ener}_{all,f} = \textstyle\sum_s \mathtt{ener}_{s,f} + \mathtt{pe}_{pow,f}, \ \mathtt{ener}_{all,all} = \textstyle\sum_s \mathtt{ener}_{s,all} + \mathtt{pet}, \ \mathtt{echg} = \mathtt{ener} - \mathtt{ener}^{base}, \ \mathtt{epct} = \mathtt{echg} / (\mathtt{ener} - \mathtt{echg})
\]
Over sector groups \(S\) (transport, buildings, industry, other energy use, power), fuels \(f\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. \(F^{pow}\) the fuel input of power generation (A4); renewables in aviation and navigation count in the subsector and group totals and in the grand total, not in a fuel total. The baseline value is scenario 1’s of the same year (Excel-AI REFCOL). Electricity demand totals (eldem) sum the subsector demand by group. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 11.


B.2.5 M4 Power
Electricity demand, generation, capacity and prices: the engineer model (standard-CPAT). Generation types \(f\): coal, gas, oil, nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, other renewables, biomass.
M4.1 Electricity demand by sector (last year’s electricity price)
\[
\mathtt{dem}_{s,t} = \mathtt{dem}_{s,t-1}\cdot \mathtt{mult}_{d(s),t}, \qquad \mathtt{pdem}_{d,t} = w_d\,\mathtt{rp}_{res,t-1} + (1 - w_d)\,\mathtt{rp}_{ind,t-1}
\]
Over sectors \(s\); \(d = d(s)\) the demand group (transport, residential, industry, services), \(w_d\) its price weight. The methodology’s form, with Excel-AI’s timing: the demand price \(\bar{p}^T\) is a blend of last year’s residential and industrial end-user prices, so power demand does not depend on this year’s power price. The methodology writes the GDP elasticity \(\epsilon_G\) (undefined there); Excel-AI uses \(\epsilon_Y\) with the income factor. Road electricity comes from the road engineer model. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Engineer model > Power demand; Excel-AI: E52-E54 (LAMBDA DEMANDMULT).
M4.2 Generation required
\[
\mathtt{req}_t = \mathtt{demtot}_t \cdot (1 + \mathtt{net}^{\dagger} + \mathtt{eiu}^{\dagger} + \mathtt{dif}^{\dagger})
\]
Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Engineer model > Power demand; Excel-AI: E57.
M4.3 Variable cost and levelised total investment cost
\[
\mathtt{tvc}_{f,t} = \mathtt{vop}^{\dagger}_{f,t} + \frac{\mathtt{fpp}_{f,t}}{\mathtt{nuu}_f} + \mathtt{ipc}^{\dagger}_{f,t} + \mathtt{ccp}_{f,t}, \qquad \mathtt{tic}_{f,t} = \mathtt{lvc}_{f,t} + \mathtt{lfx}_{f,t}
\]
Over generation types \(f\). \(\bar{p}\) is the fuel price averaged over \([t-4, t]\); \(\overline{vc}\) the levelised variable cost, a discounted average of \(vc\) from \(t\) to the last year (computed before the year loop: it depends on prices and policies only). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Power prices > Concepts 1-2; Excel-AI: E37-E43, E46.
M4.4 Dispatch between coal and gas (logit)
\[
\mathtt{lgd}_{f} = \frac{\exp(-\mathtt{K\_dispatch}^{\dagger}\cdot \mathtt{tvc}_f/\min(\mathtt{tvc}))}{\sum_{f'}\exp(-\mathtt{K\_dispatch}^{\dagger}\cdot \mathtt{tvc}_{f'}/\min(\mathtt{tvc}))}
\]
Over \(f \in\) {coal, gas}; other types run at their capacity factors. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Engineer model > Dispatch decision; Excel-AI: E57-E60 (LAMBDAs DISPATCH, LOGITW).
M4.5 Capacity
\[
\mathtt{cap}_{f,t} = \mathtt{cap}_{f,t-1} - \mathtt{ret}_{f,t-1} + \mathtt{nim}_{f,t-1}, \qquad \mathtt{ret}_{f,t} = \mathtt{cap}_{f,t} / \mathtt{lif}^{\dagger}_f
\]
Over generation types \(f\). The methodology writes the stock equation with \(g\); it is capacity. Coal retirements follow plant data where available, plus cost-based early retirement (appendix A4). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Engineer model > Retirement and capacity needed; Excel-AI: E56, E61, E62.
M4.6 Investment allocation (logit with scale-up limits)
\[
\mathtt{lgi}_{f,t} = \mathtt{zeta}^{\dagger}_f\,\frac{\exp(-\mathtt{K\_inv}^{\dagger}\cdot\mathtt{tic}_f/\min(\mathtt{tic}))}{\sum_{f'}\exp(-\mathtt{K\_inv}^{\dagger}\cdot\mathtt{tic}_{f'}/\min(\mathtt{tic}))}
\]
Over generation types \(f\). A second round allocates what the scale-up limits leave unallocated to the cheapest types (appendix A4). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Engineer model > Investment decision; Excel-AI: E63-E67 (LAMBDAs FIRSTROUND, CHEAPFILL).
M4.7 End-user electricity price
\[
\mathtt{sc}_{g,t} = \mathtt{gncav}_{t-1} + \mathtt{tmc}^{\dagger}_g, \quad \mathtt{rppre}_{g,t} = \mathtt{rppre}_{g,t-1} + \mathtt{rp.ctrl}_g\,(\mathtt{sc}_{g,t} - \mathtt{sc}_{g,t-1})(1 + \mathtt{vatr}^{\dagger}_g), \quad \mathtt{rp}_{g,t} = \mathtt{rppre}_{g,t} + (\mathtt{ccpav}_t\,\mathtt{rp.ctrl}_g\,(1 - \mathtt{rbs}) + \mathtt{pex}_{g,t})(1 + \mathtt{vatr}^{\dagger}_g)
\]
Over user groups \(g\) (residential, industry); \(gnc^{av} = \sum_f gns_f\,gnc_f\) the generation-weighted generation cost. Excel-AI’s form (data up to the last historical year, then cost changes passed through at \(pcc_g\); the supply cost uses last year’s generation cost). The methodology instead adds a markup \(mu^T\) calibrated to historical retail prices; Excel-AI’s subsidy gap \(p^0/(1+vatrate) - sp^T\) plays that role (appendix A4). \(reb\) is the rebate switch, \(pex\) the power excise. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Power prices > Concept 4; Excel-AI: E48-E51.


B.2.6 M5 Road transport (engineer model)
Excel-AI notation throughout (the methodology’s road chapter covers externalities, not the engineer model). Vehicle classes: passenger, freight, 2-3 wheelers; technologies: ICE, BEV, PHEV.
M5.1 Vehicle ownership (Gompertz target, partial adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trjhp}_t = \mathtt{trsat}\,(1 - \mathtt{fsh})\,e^{a\,e^{b\,\mathtt{gpc}_t}}, \quad \mathtt{trgtp}_t = \mathtt{trsatq}_t\,e^{a\,e^{b\,\mathtt{gpc}_t}}\,\mathtt{trjjp}_{t-1}; \ \text{ownership moves towards the target by partial adjustment, growth capped}
\]
Over vehicle classes; growth limited per year. \(y_t\) GDP per capita, \(Sat\) saturation level, \(J\) calibration to observed ownership. The only partial-adjustment equation in Excel-AI. Source: Excel-AI: Methods Transport, T1-T2 (LAMBDAs OWNDEM, GOMPTGT).
M5.2 Electric-vehicle share of purchases (logit on total cost of ownership)
\[
\mathtt{trlgn}_t = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\big(-k\,(\mathtt{trpkpbn}_t - \mathtt{trpkpin}_t)/\overline{\mathtt{tco}}_t\big)} \ \text{(ICEV share of new purchases; BEV } 1 - \mathtt{trlgn}\text{)}
\]
Over vehicle classes. Source: Excel-AI: Methods Transport (demand and choice).
M5.3 Road fuel use
\[
\mathtt{trfup}_{f,t} = \mathtt{trbkm}_{f,t} / \mathtt{fsc}_{f,t}, \quad \mathtt{trbkm}_{f,t} = \mathtt{veh}_{f,t}\cdot\mathtt{trvkc}_{f,t}/1000
\]
Over road fuels \(f\); vehicle classes \(v\). \(VKT\) vehicle-km, \(FE\) fuel use per km of the stock (Excel-AI notation). Source: Excel-AI: Methods Transport T16 (LAMBDA DEMROAD).


B.2.7 M6 Revenues
Revenue in USD million: fuel use in ktoe times \(\theta\) (PJ per ktoe) times a price component in USD/GJ.
M6.1 Revenue from new policies
\[
\mathtt{rnew}_{s,f} = \theta\,\mathtt{ener}_{s,f}\,\big(\mathtt{ctxnew}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ntx}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ets.rf}\cdot\mathtt{ets}_{s,f} + \mathtt{vatr}^{\dagger}\,(\mathtt{ctxnew}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ets}_{s,f} + \mathtt{ntx}_{s,f})\big)
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\) (power adds its own terms, appendix A6). \(\rho\) the ETS revenue factor (auctioned part; Excel-AI notation). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Fiscal revenues > Overview (\(rev = F\,\varphi\,ncp\)); Excel-AI: E73.
M6.2 Revenue from existing taxes and cost of existing subsidies
\[
\mathtt{rtx}_{s,f} = \theta\,\mathtt{ener}_{s,f}\,(\mathtt{etx} + \mathtt{vat} + \mathtt{xcpd}_{s,f}\,(1 + \mathtt{vatr}^{\dagger})), \qquad \mathtt{rsub}_{s,f} = \theta\,\mathtt{ener}_{s,f}\,\mathtt{esub}
\]
Over sectors \(s\), fuels \(f\). \(txo^{+}\) and \(txo^{-}\) are the positive (taxes) and negative (subsidies, negative) parts. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Fiscal revenues > Total revenues raised by policy; Excel-AI: E71, E72.
M6.3 Total revenue
\[
\mathtt{rtot} = \mathtt{rnet} + \mathtt{rnew} + \mathtt{rmf}, \qquad \mathtt{rnet} = \mathtt{rtx} + \mathtt{rsub}
\]
\(rev^{pow}\) power-sector revenue (appendix A6), \(rev^{mf}\) methane fee (appendix A7). Source: Excel-AI: E75, E76.


B.2.8 M7 Emissions
M7.1 Energy-related CO2
\[
\mathtt{co2}_{s,f} = \theta\,\mathtt{ener}_{s,f}\,\mathtt{ef}_{s,f}, \qquad \mathtt{co2.tot} = \sum_{s,f}\mathtt{co2}_{s,f}
\]
Over sectors \(s\) (including power: generation fuel use), fuels \(f\). \(ef\) carries the calibration to the inventory (appendix A7; off by default in Excel-AI). Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Emissions > Energy-related emissions; Excel-AI: E77, E78.
M7.2 Other greenhouse gases (pattern)
\[
\mathtt{ghg}_{u,p,t} = \mathtt{ghg}_{u,p,t-1}\cdot \mathtt{ghg.dr}_{u,t}
\]
Over UNFCCC sectors \(u\), gases \(p\). Each source grows with its driver (energy CO2, industrial energy CO2, GDP and population with elasticities); the source equations are in appendix A7. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Emissions (N2O, IPPU, agriculture, LULUCF, waste); Excel-AI: E80-E86.


B.2.9 M8 GDP
Excel-AI notation throughout: the methodology describes the multipliers but gives no in-model equation.
M8.1 Fiscal space and impulse
\[
\mathtt{fis.rev} = \mathtt{rnet} + \mathtt{rnew} + \mathtt{rsr} + \mathtt{rpsu} + \mathtt{ch4.rev}, \quad \mathtt{fis.sp}_t = \frac{\mathtt{fis.rev}_t - \mathtt{fis.ref}_t}{\mathtt{gdp.usd}_t \cdot 1000}, \quad \mathtt{fis.imp}_t = \mathtt{fis.sp}_t - \mathtt{fis.sp}_{t-1}\frac{\mathtt{gdp.usd}_{t-1}}{\mathtt{gdp.usd}_t}
\]
Excel-AI notation: the revenue is the whole fiscal balance of the energy taxes and subsidies (existing, new, price-control wedges, producer subsidies, methane fee), against the baseline (\(\mathtt{fis.ref}\)); the impulse starts in GDPStartYear (in the base year it is the whole fiscal space). \(\mathtt{fis.impp}\) is the impulse from the carbon-pricing start year (CPIntro), used for the recycled revenue. \(\mathtt{fis.lag}_{l}\), \(\mathtt{fis.lagp}_{l}\) hold the impulses of the 19 earlier years. Source: Excel-AI: E91, E92; Mitigation section 16.
M8.2 GDP effect of the revenue and of its use
\[
\mathtt{gdp.eff}_t = \textstyle\sum_i \mathtt{fis.eff}_{i,t}\,[\mathtt{GDPEndogenous}], \quad \mathtt{fis.eff}_{exc,t} = -\textstyle\sum_{k}\mathtt{fis.imp}_{t-k}\,m_{exc}(k), \quad \mathtt{fis.eff}_{i,t} = \frac{\mathtt{EXP}_i}{100}\textstyle\sum_{k}\mathtt{fis.impp}_{t-k}\,m_i(k)
\]
Over uses of revenue \(i\) (labour tax cut EXPLabortax, corporate tax cut EXPCIT, public investment EXPCapex, goods and services EXPGoodsandserv, transfers EXPTransfers); the revenue itself with the excise multiplier. Multipliers \(m_i(k)\) by lag from appendix A8.1. Applied only if GDPEndogenous = Yes. \(\mathtt{gdpg}_{i,t} = (1 + g^0_t)(\mathtt{fis.eff}_{i,t-1} - \mathtt{fis.eff}_{i,t-2}) / \mathtt{gdp.lvl}_{t-1}\): each instrument’s contribution to GDP growth (memo). Source: methodology: 04_Multipliers; Excel-AI: E93, E94; Mitigation section 16.
M8.3 GDP feedback, one year later
\[
\mathtt{gdp.lvl}_t = 1 + \mathtt{gdp.eff}_{t-1}, \qquad \mathtt{gdp.pos.usd}_t = \mathtt{gdp.usd}^{0}_t\,\mathtt{gdp.lvl}_t, \qquad 1 + \mathtt{gdp.pos.pct}_t = (1 + \mathtt{gdp.base}_t)\,\frac{\mathtt{gdp.lvl}_t}{\mathtt{gdp.lvl}_{t-1}}
\]
The only link from year \(t\) to year \(t+1\) other than lags of a block’s own quantities. Revenue of year \(t\) moves GDP from \(t+1\) (root NORMS 5c). Source: Excel-AI: E95.


B.2.10 D Distribution
One analysis year \(y\); households \(j\), deciles \(d\), consumption categories \(g\), fuels \(f \in g\) (methodology chapter 5).
D1.1 Budget shares
\[
\mathtt{bsh}_{g,d,s} = \text{HHSurvey } \langle g\rangle\text{\_share of } \texttt{bsh.<bkt|dec>.<s>.<stat>.<q>}
\]
Over fuels and categories \(g\) (8 fuels, 14 categories, biomass), deciles \(d\) and the basket; samples \(s\) overall, urban, rural. The survey tables hold the decile statistics; Coded CPAT reads them (QuantilesStatistic: mean or median). Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_1; Excel-AI: Distribution section 5 (HHSurvey).
D1.2 Indirect price change of consumption categories (input-output)
\[
\mathtt{gfac}_k = \frac{\mathtt{grev}_k}{\mathtt{gtot}_k}, \quad \mathtt{grev}_k = \textstyle\sum_{f \in k} \mathtt{spend}_f\,\mathtt{dpa}_f, \quad \mathtt{dpr}_g = \textstyle\sum_k \mathtt{DLcat}_{g,k}\,\mathtt{gfac}_k
\]
Over fuel groups \(k\) (coal, electricity, gas, crude oil, oil products), categories \(g\). Excel-AI uses GTAP’s total-requirement (Leontief) coefficients \(L\) directly, weighted by household demand \(H\) of the GTAP sectors in each category; the base-year spending \(S_f\) on each fuel (pav.sp) at the industrial price change \(t^a_f\), over the group’s total use \(U_k\) (B1.1). With ScaleGTAP = No, \(U_k\) is the spending itself. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_3; Excel-AI: Distribution section 3; DistMapping DLcat, DIOTot.
D1.3 Price change by fuel from mitigation
\[
\mathtt{dpr}_{f.res} = \frac{\mathtt{atp.res}_{f,y}}{\mathtt{atp.res}^{B}_{f,y}} - 1 \ (\mathtt{rp.res.ecy} \text{ for electricity}), \qquad \mathtt{dpa}_f = \frac{\mathtt{rpn}_{f,y}}{\mathtt{rpn}^{B}_{f,y}} - 1 \ (\mathtt{rp.ind.ecy})
\]
Over household fuels \(f\) (direct effect); fuels by industrial or average price (indirect effect, D1.2). Analysis year \(y\) = YearDistn; the baseline is scenario 1. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, sec 5.3.1, eq-5_8; Excel-AI: Distribution section 2 (FromMitigation).
D1.4 Direct, indirect and total effect
\[
\mathtt{fac}_{i} = \mathtt{dpr}_i\,(1 + \mathtt{dpr}_i)^{\mathtt{eps}_i}, \quad \mathtt{def}_f = -\mathtt{fac}_f\,\mathtt{bsh}_f\,\mathtt{lscale}, \quad \mathtt{ief}_g = -\mathtt{fac}_g\,\mathtt{bsh}_g\,\mathtt{lscale}, \quad \mathtt{tef.tot} = \mathtt{def.tot} + \mathtt{ief.tot}
\]
Over fuels and categories \(i\), deciles \(d\), samples. In % of consumption. The elasticity factor applies when PEDs = Yes (behavioural response, eq-5_7); \(\lambda\) = lscale (B1.3); the cooking fuel is exempt for the poorest deciles where chosen (B1.4). Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_2, eq-5_7; Excel-AI: Distribution sections 4 and 6.
D1.5 Revenue recycling, targeted transfer
\[
\mathtt{tgt}_d = \mathtt{tgtamt}\,\mathtt{recv}_d\,\mathtt{tgtw}_d\,\mathtt{medflag}_d, \quad \mathtt{tgtamt} = \frac{\mathtt{rtgt}}{\sum_d \mathtt{recv}_d\,\mathtt{tgtw}_d\,\mathtt{pop\_tot\_adj}_d}, \quad \mathtt{rtgt} = \mathtt{rev}\cdot\mathtt{EXPTransfers}
\]
Over deciles \(d\). \(R\) new revenue (rnew \(\times\) xr, local currency), \(\sigma_T\) the transfer share; \(\tau_d\) the share of the decile’s population under the targeted percentile (popsh, popcum), \(cov\), \(leak\) the coverage and leakage rates. The weight \(w_d\) is 1, the poverty-line share (TargetBelow) or the ASPIRE programme’s benefit by quintile (TransferType). Other recycling options in B1.5 and B1.6. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_9 to eq-5_12; Excel-AI: Distribution section 8.
D1.6 Net effect by decile
\[
\mathtt{rec.tot}_d = \frac{\mathtt{pit}_d + \mathtt{pui}_d + \mathtt{cts}_d + \mathtt{tgt}_d}{\mathtt{cons\_pc\_na}_d}\cdot 100, \qquad \mathtt{net.tot}_d = \mathtt{tef.tot}_d + \mathtt{rec.tot}_d
\]
Over deciles \(d\), samples. Per person, in % of consumption per person scaled to national accounts (B1.2). Consumption effects are Laspeyres (upper-bound) estimates unless PEDs = Yes. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, sec 5.4; Excel-AI: Distribution section 9.

title: Appendix B — Equation list: CPAT code names
text:
B.3 Adjustments: mitigation
Started; completed block by block before each block is coded (coded/TODO.md phase 0). Sources for each block: excel_ai/mitigation/Equations.md, Equations_addendum.md and Formulas.md (the workbook formulas), and the Methods chapters in excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/.

B.3.1 A1 Policies
To complete: ETS (coverage, benchmarks, cap, semi-elasticity, fast price estimate, override, volatility adjustment: E4-E13); fuel-price reform path (E2); feebates (E3); existing carbon pricing growth (E17); methane fee (E18); exemptions (E18a); subsidy and price-control phase-outs; Pigouvian components (R3).
A1.1 ETS fast price estimate (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ets.est}_t = \frac{\ln(\mathtt{ets.cap}_t / \mathtt{ets.bce}_t)}{\mathtt{ets.se}_t\cdot \mathtt{ets.vadj}}
\]
Excel-AI notation. \(bce\) is the baseline CO2 of the covered sectors: Excel-AI’s stored scenario-1 values (sheet BaselineCO2), read as data until the baseline pass computes them (user 2026-10-29). Source: Excel-AI: E7-E11.
A1.2 Pigouvian taxes and existing pre-tax wedges (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{airpol.mc}_{s,f}, \ \mathtt{pig.ap}_c, \ \mathtt{cc.code}_c, \ \mathtt{pig.tr}_c = \textstyle\sum_k \mathtt{pig.trb}_{k}\,\mathtt{pig.trg}_{k}, \ \mathtt{pigx}_c = \mathtt{pig.phi}\,(\cdots), \ \mathtt{xcpb}_c, \ \mathtt{xpre}_c = \mathtt{txo} + \mathtt{pcsw} + \mathtt{ppcw} + \mathtt{xcpb}
\]
Over subsectors \(s\) and fuels \(f\) (air pollution), price codes \(c\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 1, rows 185-418). Air pollution: the value of averted PM2.5 \(v_t\) (air pollution module, typed FromAirPollution; the base year reads the next year) times the module’s concentration coefficients \(\kappa\) of the source (road, ground level, food, other; coal, gas and other power plants) times the combustion factors, per GJ; by price code weighted by base-year fuel use (residential coal only above ApCoalResMin of buildings use), per unit for oil products. Transport: accident, congestion and road-damage cost per km (typed FromTransportCB) relative to the base year, times base-year fuel economy, the elasticity share of usage and the road share of the fuel. Climate: the national SCC times the generic CO2 factor (Inputs rows 316-322). \(\phi_t\) phases the tax in over AddEfficientTaxesPhaseInYears from CPIntro. xcpb: existing carbon pricing against the year embedded in the price data. The tax enters ntxg only if AddEfficientTaxes = Yes (not in Coded CPAT yet). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (rows 185-418).


B.3.2 A2 Prices
To complete: last historical year and price data; excise floor (E22); split of taxes and subsidies by sign (E23); producer subsidy (R7); existing carbon pricing level and change (E30); VAT on oil products by household share; other oil products (L13).
A2.1 Excise floor (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{txo}_t = \max(\mathtt{txo}_L,\ \mathtt{txf}_t) \text{ if } \mathtt{txo}_L \ge 0
\]
\(\widetilde{txo}\) is the floating value of M2.2; \(L\) the last historical price year. Source: Excel-AI: E22.
A2.2 Change in existing carbon pricing (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{xcp}_{s,f,t} = \mathtt{ef}_{s,f}\,(\mathtt{XT}^{\dagger}\cdot \mathtt{xct.p}_t + \mathtt{XE}^{\dagger}\cdot \mathtt{xets.p}_t), \qquad \mathtt{xcpd}_{s,f,t} = \mathtt{xcp}_{s,f,t} - \mathtt{ef}_{s,f}\,\mathtt{XCP0}^{\dagger}_{s,f}
\]
\(t^* = \min(t, T_x)\), \(T_x\) the last data year; \(XCP^0\) the existing carbon pricing already in the price data. Source: methodology: 03_Mitigation, Appendix C (existing carbon price); Excel-AI: E17, E30.
A2.3 International energy prices by source (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{gp}_{k,t} = \mathtt{gpn}_{k,t}\,\mathtt{defl}_t \cdot \{1, \mathtt{gp.hi}_k, \mathtt{gp.lo}_k\}_{t > L}
\]
Over sources \(s\) (IMF, WB, IEA, EIA; averages AVG, IMF-IEA, IMF-WB; Manual), commodities \(k\) (oil, coal, gas LNG, North America, Europe, global, Europe shifting to LNG). Excel-AI notation. \(T^{s,k}\) the first extended year of the series, \(\pi^{US}\) US GDP deflator inflation. Averages skip missing sources; global gas is the average of LNG, North America and Europe; Manual: IMF to 2025, then the manual path. Excel-AI reads the World Bank gas rows by position (its LNG is the Europe series and the reverse). Past its data (2041 on) the IEA series reads a misaligned cell in Excel-AI (issue I152); Python leaves it missing. Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_pint (build_inputs_pint); Mitigation section 2 (gpn, gp).
A2.4 Historical domestic prices and forecasting coefficients (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{sp}_y,\ \mathtt{txo}_y\ (y \le L),\quad \mathtt{spf} = \mathtt{fixsp},\quad \mathtt{pcc} = \text{bucket}(\mathtt{ps}^{data}_{t_0})
\]
Over price fuels; historical years \(y\) 2021 to \(L\). Excel-AI notation: \(\gamma\) GJ per price unit, \(\nu\) the CPI index. Pass-through: the base-year data bucketed (up to PassLo 0, up to PassHi PassMid, else 1; biomass 1), or the manual price control, or 1 (GovPriceControls). VAT: the data rate where filled, else the general rate for consumers (residential coal and gas, oil products) and 0 otherwise, times the household share of the oil product. Coal and gas margins are read at 2024 (issue I101). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_prices (build_inputs_prices).
A2.5 Producer subsidies (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{psu}_{f,t} = -\mathtt{pros}_{f,t}\cdot 10^6 / \mathtt{psd}_{f,t};\quad \mathtt{ps}_{c,t} = \mathtt{psu}_{f(c),t}\,(\text{litres per barrel for other oil products}) / \gamma_c
\]
Over producer fuels \(f\) (oil, coal, gas, biomass). Excel-AI notation. \(PROS\) producer subsidy (data, USD m real, held after \(L\)), \(D\) the demand it is spread over: world production (oil), the average of world production and domestic use (coal, gas), domestic use (biomass). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 1 (pros, psd, psu), section 2 (ps).
A2.6 Prices averaged over fuel use (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{pnq}_c, \ \mathtt{pctx}, \mathtt{etsnew}, \mathtt{pntx}, \mathtt{pxcd}, \mathtt{rpn}_c \ (\text{use-weighted}), \ \mathtt{pnce} = \mathtt{rpn} - \mathtt{pbc}, \ \mathtt{pvatn}; \quad \mathtt{pav.uv}_f, \ \mathtt{pav.las}_f, \ \mathtt{pav.time}_f, \ \mathtt{pav.mix}_f, \ \mathtt{pav.leg}_f, \ \mathtt{pav.idx}_f
\]
Over price codes \(c\) (fuel and price sector), fuels \(f\) including electricity and the total, years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 2, filled in the year loop because it reads fuel use). By price code: new carbon tax, ETS, new taxes, existing carbon pricing and after-tax price averaged over the subsectors that use the code (the pre-tax build-up pbc where no subsector does); VAT on new policies is the remainder. By fuel: unit value, Laspeyres index at scenario-1 quantities, time index at base-year quantities, mix effect; the legacy index (AveragePriceMethod = Legacy): coal and gas weight residential, industry and power (generation cost) prices by scenario-1 quantities, oil products take the single price, the rest the unit value. Electricity uses the user tariffs and consumption; the total converts electricity at GJ per kWh. rpe = the average price of all energy. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 2 (rows pnq-rpn, pav., pavl.*, rpe).


B.3.3 A3 Fuel use
To complete: initially exempt use from the household survey (ExemptMostCook, R6); self-generated renewables; income elasticity adjustment.
A3.1 Elasticities of the country (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ela}[k|f|g] \text{ for } k \in \{\mathtt{inc}, \mathtt{usg}, \mathtt{eff}, \mathtt{aei}\}
\]
Over fuel groups \(f\) (coal, gas, gasoline, diesel, oil, biomass, renewables, electricity), sector groups \(g\) (transport, residential, industry, services). Excel-AI notation: income \(Y\), own-price usage \(U\) and efficiency \(F\) elasticities, autonomous efficiency improvement \(\alpha\). Several rows reuse another fuel’s or sector’s legacy row (core/excel_ai/elasticity_rows.csv). Manual elasticities (MTInputs ElIncMainSrc, ElPrcMainSrc) are not in Coded CPAT yet. Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_ela (build_inputs_ela).
A3.2 The fuel | subsector table (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ey}, \mathtt{eu}, \mathtt{ef}, \mathtt{alpha}, \mathtt{co2ef}, \mathtt{ener0}, \mathtt{xcp0}, \mathtt{vat}
\]
Over fuels \(f\), subsectors \(s\). Excel-AI notation: elasticities of the fuel’s elasticity fuel and the subsector’s elasticity sector (residential biomass income elasticity 0 unless BiomassNormal, I24); CO2 factor of the subsector’s EF sector, calibrated; base-year fuel use from the energy balance (flow 1 plus signed flow 2) or EnergyCons (BalancesOrConsumption); the existing carbon pricing embedded in the price data, by ECP sector; non-CO2 factors; positions of the road model and residential leakage rows. Source: Excel-AI: Inputs rows 5-148.
A3.3 Biofuels in road transport, renewables in aviation and navigation (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trbe}_{rod,bgs|bdi}, \ \mathtt{trbe}_{rod,obf} \ (\mathtt{trbea}, \text{oil | transport elasticities}), \ \mathtt{trbe}_{rod,bio}; \quad \mathtt{ener}_{avi|nav,ren,t} = \mathtt{ener}_{t-1}\,\mathtt{trrena}\,\Psi_t (1 + \mathtt{GDPI}_t)^{\epsilon_Y} r_t^{\epsilon_U + \epsilon_F(1+\epsilon_U)}, \ r_t = \mathtt{trpren}_t / \mathtt{trpren}_{t-1}
\]
Over years \(t\) after the base year. Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 5b). Biogasoline and biodiesel are blended: they follow the road use of the fossil fuel. Other biofuels follow M3.1 with the oil | transport elasticities and the road biomass price. Base year: the energy balance road flow (bgs, bdi, obf) or EnergyCons (BalancesOrConsumption). Renewables in aviation and navigation (base year EnergyCons enc.ren) follow M3.1 with the renewables | transport elasticities and the price ratio of the solar investment cost (trpren = tic pow sol); the efficiency factors use AdditionalEfficiencyRoadVehicle. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b (trp.eb2, trbe, trbea, trpren, trrena, trp.rn0).
A3.4 Residential leakage to biomass (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{lkt}_f = \mathtt{nce}_{res,f}(1 + vat_f), \ \mathtt{lkp}_f, \ \mathtt{lkd}_f, \ \mathtt{lkb}_f, \ \mathtt{lkc}_{f,t} = \mathtt{lkc}_{f,t-1} + \mathtt{lkd}_{f,t} + \Delta\mathtt{lkxa}_{f,t}, \ \mathtt{lkcb}_t = \mathtt{lkcb}_{t-1} + \textstyle\sum_f \mathtt{lkb}_{f,t}
\]
Over residential fuels \(f\) that may leak (gas, LPG, kerosene), years \(t\) after the base year. Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 6b). On only for the country’s most-used cooking fuel (WHO) and when BiomassLeakage = Yes (off in Egypt’s scenarios). \(\tau\) the new taxes per GJ with VAT, \(\sigma\) the substitution elasticity of biomass for LPG, \(\eta\) stove efficiencies (NatGasEff, LPGEff, KerEff, BioEff), \(L\) the substitution lag (ResSubstLag). \(X\) the initially exempt use (lkx), phased out over ExemptPhaseoutPeriod from YearPha when ExemptPhaseout; ExemptMostCook = Yes needs the household survey and is not in Coded CPAT yet. The cumulative changes enter residential fuel use (M3.2). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 6b (lkt to lks).
A3.5 Road engineer model, data (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trshf}, \mathtt{trfe}, \mathtt{trown}, \mathtt{trvkd}, \mathtt{trevp}, \mathtt{trevo}, \mathtt{trdut}, \mathtt{trimp}, \mathtt{trusd}, \mathtt{trchs}, \mathtt{trsat}, \mathtt{trfeb}, \mathtt{trcpp}, \mathtt{trfen}, \mathtt{trvp}; \quad \mathtt{trp.bsh}_{c,f}, \ \mathtt{trp.tax}_c, \ \mathtt{trp.bus}, \ \mathtt{trp.*}
\]
Over vehicle classes \(c\) (passenger cars, light vehicles, freight vehicles, 2-3 wheelers, buses), road fuels \(f\) (gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. Country data by year (shares of road fuel use by vehicle class, fuel economy, ownership per thousand people, distance per vehicle, EV shares of purchases and of the stock, duties, import and used-vehicle shares, charging stations, ownership saturation) exist for the data years only (TrYr: 2022-2025); vehicle prices hold their last value; BEV fuel economy and the charging cost follow global paths. The parameters are the transport parameters (TransportParams), the road rows of the fuel | subsector table (gj, lambda = litres per ktoe, CO2 per litre, elasticities, AEEI, base-year use), duties and VAT of the customs data year, import shares of the import data year, range anxiety (Transport3, fitted values where the country has them). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b rows 3611-3816 (TransportParams, Transport1, Transport2, Transport3, TransportPaths, Manual inputs BEV fuel economy).
A3.6 Road engineer model, vehicle stock and ownership (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{tropn}, \mathtt{tropu}, \mathtt{tropf}, \mathtt{tropc}; \ \mathtt{travn}, \mathtt{trretn}, \mathtt{traftn}; \ \mathtt{trjhp}, \mathtt{trjjp}, \mathtt{trgtp}, \mathtt{trdemp}, \mathtt{trdmcp}, \mathtt{trbyt}, \mathtt{trbytn}, \mathtt{trbytu}; \ \mathtt{trbuyn}, \mathtt{trplgn}, \mathtt{trclon} \ (\text{and the freight, 2-3 wheeler rows}); \ \mathtt{trsta}, \mathtt{trmku}, \mathtt{trpev}, \mathtt{trra}
\]
Over vehicle classes \(c\) (new and used passenger vehicles, freight, 2-3 wheelers; ICEV and BEV), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (vehicles per thousand people). Retirements: the average stock of the last \(n = \min(N_c, t - t_0 + 1)\) years over the life \(N_c\). Ownership demand: Gompertz in GDP per capita after the GDP feedback (a = gomp_a, b = own_gomp_b), scaled by the actual/expected ratio \(J\) of the data years, partial adjustment \(\mu\) (own_adj), growth and decline bounds; freight takes its share \(\phi\) of the saturation level, falling with income towards fre_share_target; 2-3 wheelers follow a hump in income (cyc_peak_inc, cyc_scale). Purchases split new/used by the used-vehicle share; in data years the gap to the data stock closes the balance (trplg). Charging stations grow with the BEV stock and fall with their cost (charging-station subsidy); the charging mark-up falls with the EV share of the stock; range anxiety is held for TrRALag years, then falls with the stations. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b rows 3839-3999, 4236-4249 (trsps to trstdc, tropn to trbevm, trcss to trra, trjhp to trbytu).
A3.7 Road engineer model, total cost of ownership and EV choice (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trdkmpasi} = -PV(\mathtt{trdisc}, N, \mathtt{trvkna}); \ \mathtt{trppip}, \mathtt{trdppin}, \mathtt{tranpin}, \mathtt{trsvpin}, \mathtt{trimpin}, \mathtt{trfupin}, \mathtt{trtopin}, \mathtt{trpkpin}; \ \mathtt{trppbp} \ldots \mathtt{trpkpbn} \ (+ \mathtt{trra}); \ \mathtt{trppui} \ldots \mathtt{trpkpbu}; \ \mathtt{trtcav}, \mathtt{trlgn}, \mathtt{trshn}, \mathtt{trlgu}, \mathtt{trshu}, \mathtt{trevsh}; \ \mathtt{trfbvpi}, \mathtt{trpvp}, \mathtt{tradvpi}, \mathtt{trcuep}, \mathtt{trvatbp}, \mathtt{trsubp}, \mathtt{trdtxp}
\]
Over vehicle classes (new and used passenger vehicles, freight, 2-3 wheelers), ICEV and BEV, years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. Purchase price P with duties x import share, VAT, ad-valorem taxes (baseline or policy), BEV subsidies and the feebate (CO2 intensity minus the pivot, average or manual, times the feebate rate and the discounted distance); first-year depreciation d, annuity of the rest over N - 1 years, salvage value SV, insurance (rate iota, factor theta = ins_factor), maintenance m per km, fuel or electricity (with the charging mark-up) per km plus the distance tax; BEVs add range anxiety. The discount rate falls with GDP per capita between disc_max and disc_min. In data years the purchase shares are the data’s; the logit gives them afterwards (k by vehicle class). Excel-AI uses the ICEV’s discounted distance in the freight BEV feebate (row 4197) and the BEV’s capital cost with the ICEV’s insurance and maintenance for plug-in hybrids (row 4175). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b rows 4081-4233, 4250-4263, 4318-4323, 4352-4357.
A3.8 Road engineer model, fuel economy, distance and fuel use (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trfn}, \mathtt{trfna}, \mathtt{trint}, \mathtt{trfso}, \mathtt{trfsc}, \mathtt{trvku0}, \mathtt{trbkm0}, \mathtt{trfu0}; \ \mathtt{trbu}, \mathtt{trcq}, \mathtt{trdfp}, \mathtt{trdff}, \mathtt{trdfc}; \ \mathtt{trvkc}, \mathtt{trbkm}, \mathtt{trfup}, \mathtt{trelp}, \mathtt{trfuf}, \mathtt{trelf}, \mathtt{trfuc}, \mathtt{trelc}; \ \mathtt{trbusf}, \mathtt{trbusel}; \ \mathtt{tricp}, \mathtt{tricn}, \mathtt{trico}, \mathtt{tricw}, \mathtt{trveh}
\]
Over vehicle classes \(c\), fuels \(f\) (gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas, plug-in hybrid, electricity), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. New-vehicle fuel economy responds to the fuel price with the feebate (\(\beta\) the feebate rate, \(e\) the fossil CO2 per litre); the stock turns over at \(\tau\) (passenger: 1 / the weighted ownership life; freight, 2-3 wheelers: 1 / life). ICE fuel shares of purchases follow the TCO ratio of the fuel (own elasticity) and of the other fuels (cross elasticity), then the stock shares turn over. Distance per vehicle is the data’s in data years, then responds to the cost per km and to GDP per capita; the base year calibrates distance to the energy balance (trbu, trcq: held after the base year). Buses: base-year bus fuel use scaled with passenger fuel use. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b rows 4003-4078, 4264-4522.
A3.9 Road engineer model, results (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{trcf2}, \mathtt{trcf2e}, \mathtt{trkt}_f, \mathtt{trbio}, \mathtt{trkte}, \mathtt{trsum}; \ \mathtt{trkmp}, \mathtt{trfcp}, \mathtt{trafg}, \mathtt{trafo}, \mathtt{trafe}, \mathtt{trvht}; \ \mathtt{trrafp}, \mathtt{trraff}, \mathtt{trrafc}; \ \mathtt{trq}, \mathtt{tran.rsh}
\]
Over road fuels \(f\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. Road fuel use of the engineer model in ktoe, calibrated to the base-year balance (electricity only if recon_ele); it replaces road fuel use of section 5 and road electricity demand of section 3 where TrModel = Engineer (tr.sw = 1; Coded CPAT since 1.1.0p1.4; Egypt’s shipped scenarios use the elasticity model). Distance, fuel use and stock-average fuel economy by vehicle class, the range-anxiety fit targets of the data years, and road fuel use with its share of total use (trq, tran.rsh) go to the transport co-benefits module. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 5b rows 4525-4616.


B.3.4 A4 Power
To complete: capacity factors and overrides; vintages of capital cost and storage (E34-E36); VRE share and storage (methodology: \(sst = 9v^2\), long-term storage above 75%); early coal retirement (E62); investment need (E63, \(Req_t^2/Req_{t-1}\)); second-round investment; manual capacity; PPAs; supply cost lag (E48); subsidy gap; renewable subsidies and rebates.
A4.1 Generation types of the country (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{cax0}, \mathtt{life}, \mathtt{opfx}, \mathtt{vop}, \mathtt{cf}, \mathtt{eff}, \mathtt{wacc}, \mathtt{dlf} = \frac{1 - (1+r)^{-N}}{1 - (1+r)^{-1}}
\]
Over generation types \(k\) (coal, gas, oil, nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, other renewables, biomass). Excel-AI notation. Costs, lifetime and capacity factor of the legacy Power table (country where positive, else world); efficiency and capacity factor from the base-year energy balance and installed capacity; WACC by WACCSource (country rate plus the coal or technology premium of the income group, the studies value, a user or income-group rate, at least MinimumWACC). Investment permitted (If Present*: when the type has more than InvPresentShare of capacity) and its first year (hydro from the base year when it has more than HydInvShare of generation). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_ptech, Inputs_pset (build_inputs_powerdata).
A4.2 Power year paths (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{tcf}_{k,t}, \mathtt{cbat}_t, \mathtt{cel}_t, \mathtt{incp}_t, \mathtt{incf}_t, \mathtt{shock}_t, \mathtt{pret}_{coa,t}
\]
Over years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. Capex time factors of the RenewableCostDeclineRate scenario for renewables (missing series: the old series for wind and solar, medium otherwise), medium for the others; income factor a quartic polynomial in log GDP per capita of the previous year; demand shock of 2023-2024 (GHGs data); planned coal retirement where the data flag it. Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_ppath (build_inputs_powerdata).
A4.3 Power parameters and system shares (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{req\_factor} = (1 + s_{nxp} + s_{tsd} + s_{eou} + s_{add})\,\kappa \cdot 1000 / 8760
\]
Excel-AI notation. \(D\) final electricity demand of the base year (energy balance), \(G\) base-year generation (ktoe). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs_ppar; Inputs rows 254-263.
A4.4 Derived constants of the generation types, user and demand groups (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{acap}, \mathtt{afix}, \mathtt{lcap}, \mathtt{lfix}, \mathtt{k}, \mathtt{efk}, \mathtt{xcp0}; \quad \mathtt{aeef}_d = (1 + \alpha_d + a)^{-(1+\epsilon^U_d)}
\]
Excel-AI notation: \(\bar{s}\) the average outstanding share of capital (CapAvgShr). User groups (residential, industry): transmission cost, pass-through, VAT and historical prices; demand groups (transport, residential, industry, services): electricity elasticities and the efficiency multiple; base-year demand by subsector from the energy balance or EnergyCons (BalancesOrConsumption). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs rows 204-252 (build_inputs_power).
A4.5 Scenario settings of the generation types, variable and levelised variable cost (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{tvc}_{k,t} = \mathtt{vbc} + \mathtt{xac} + \mathtt{shk} + \mathtt{reb}, \quad \mathtt{lvc}_{k,t} = \frac{d_t\,\mathtt{tvcx}_t + (\mathtt{dsum}_t - d_t)\,\mathtt{lvc}_{t+1}}{\mathtt{dsum}_t}
\]
Over generation types \(k\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation. The scenario’s A0 settings: capacity factor (actual within CFOverride bounds, else the studies value), efficiency (actual above MinimumThermalEfficiency), WACC by WACCSource. \(\bar{p}^f\): the price before new policies of the type’s fuel, the average over the year and up to PwAvgLag years before (spot prices if chosen); \(xck\) the change in existing carbon pricing against the price data, \(cic\) the coal implicit cost (GoalSeekCoal, short to long term by CoalICYr), \(xac\) new carbon tax, ETS cost and the new taxes of the fuel price reform per kWh, \(shk\) the shadow price, \(reb\) the rebate of the shadow price. The levelised variable cost discounts the remaining years at the type’s WACC. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (A0, B, C, D).
A4.6 Power cost breakdown (memo) (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{pcbcap}, \mathtt{pcbom}, \mathtt{pcbfu}, \mathtt{pcbcp}, \mathtt{pcbrns}, \mathtt{pcbchk}
\]
Excel-AI notation: levelised capital cost, fixed and variable O&M, fuel and existing carbon pricing, new policy costs, renewable subsidy; the check against the cost used. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (cost breakdown).
A4.7 Electricity excise and renewable subsidies of the scenario (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{entx}_{u,t}, \mathtt{rnsp}_t, \mathtt{rns}_{k,t}, \mathtt{exs}_t = \mathtt{gint}\cdot \mathtt{cptraj}_t \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{electricity excise scenario}]
\]
Excel-AI notation. The manual excise path applies with AdditionalExcise (nominal inputs deflated); the additional renewable subsidy phases out over RenSubsidyAddPhaseoutYrs from its start year; hydro by RenewableSubsidyHydro. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (entxd, entx, rnsp, rns, exs).
A4.8 End-user electricity prices, subsidies and power-sector taxes (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{rp}_{u,t}, \mathtt{rppre}_{u,t}, \mathtt{sc}_{u,t} = \mathtt{gncav}_{t-1} + \mathtt{tmc}_u, \mathtt{pseu}, \mathtt{ores}, \mathtt{csd}, \mathtt{txe}, \mathtt{rpnv}
\]
Over user groups \(u\) (residential, industry). Excel-AI notation. Historical years: the data price; after the last historical year the price moves with the supply cost (average generation cost of last year plus transmission), the producer subsidy per kWh, the consumer subsidy phase-out and the other residual, passed through at PowerSectorPriceChangePassOn; new policy costs (\(\bar{c}\) the share-weighted policy cost per kWh, rebated if chosen) and the excise of the scenario. Producer subsidies are split between the groups by their supply-cost gap (floor PsElFloor). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (G1, G2).
A4.9 Early retirement and second-round investment (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{early}, \mathtt{egrow}, \mathtt{ecshr}, \mathtt{second}, \mathtt{deficit}, \mathtt{dgas}
\]
Excel-AI notation: coal retires early up to EarlyMaxShare of its effective capacity, as far as wind and solar can grow and are cheaper (logit share \(s^{ec}\)); the investment need left after the logit allocation goes to the cheapest permitted types with space under their scale-up limit (ties broken by the type order), the rest to gas if PwDeficitGas. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (K4, K5, investment).


B.3.5 A5 Road transport
To complete from Methods Transport (T1-T18): retirement, purchases new and used, total cost of ownership, ICE fuel split, new and stock fuel economy, vehicle-km, calibration, buses, range anxiety (fitted offline), biofuels.


B.3.6 A6 Revenues
To complete: power-sector revenues (E75: fuel taxes of generation, excise, VAT on electricity, subsidy gap, renewable subsidies, rebates); subsidy reform revenue; producer subsidies; price-control losses (memo).
A6.1 Power-sector revenues by generation type (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{prtx}, \mathtt{prsub}, \mathtt{prxc}, \mathtt{prnew}, \mathtt{prxl}, \mathtt{prrns}
\]
Excel-AI notation: existing taxes and subsidies on power fuels, the new policy cost of generation less the free part of the ETS, existing carbon pricing, renewable subsidies. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 3 (revenues).
A6.2 Revenue by policy instrument (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{covct}_e = \textstyle\sum_f \mathtt{co2}_{e,f}\,\mathtt{ctcov}_f\,[\mathtt{ctr}_e > 0], \ \mathtt{rpol}_{ct,exc,exi,vat,ets,psu,ren,mf,trs,ctp,etp,tot}, \ \mathtt{rfu}_f, \ \mathtt{rfg}_{pow,f}, \ \mathtt{rpct} = R / GDP
\]
Over coverage sectors \(e\), fuels \(f\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 12). Carbon tax on covered CO2 (power: coal, gas, oil), electricity rebates and excise surplus; excises net of the power carbon tax and ETS; VAT; ETS at the auctioned share \(\rho\); producer subsidies and the power subsidy gap; renewable subsidies; the methane fee; existing taxes as the remainder. Revenue by fuel and by power fuel; shares of GDP; nominal GDP from WEO divided by Billion (the WEO values are already in billions). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 12; covct section 17.


B.3.7 A7 Emissions
To complete: local air pollutants by sector (section 15, E87-E90).
A7.1 Emission factors of the country (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{EFSel}[f|s] \cdot \mathtt{EFCalib}
\]
Over fuels \(f\), EF sectors \(s\) (power, road, residential, industry; jet fuel in aviation). Excel-AI notation. Some rows read another fuel or sector (\(f'\), \(s'\)); jet fuel takes the IEA factor, biomass 0. The calibration factor \(\chi\) uses Excel-AI’s stored scenario-1 CO2 (user 2026-10-29). Other combustion pollutants (GAINS, t/ktoe): country, else region, else world, else 0; other energy use the largest factor of the fuel across the subsectors above it (issue I149). Source: Excel-AI: Inputs rows 273-312, 933-1471; Settings C26-C30.
A7.2 Greenhouse gases by UNFCCC category (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ghg}_{c,g}, \ \mathtt{ghg.dr}_c, \ \mathtt{ghg.k}_{enr,ch4}, \ \mathtt{ghg.flr}, \ \mathtt{ghg.m}, \ \mathtt{ghg.gi}, \ \mathtt{pop}, \ \mathtt{gdppc.g}
\]
Over categories \(c\) (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, LULUCF, waste, other), gases \(g\) (CO2, CH4, N2O, F-gases), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 14). Energy CO2 is the model’s plus flaring; energy CH4 is combustion and fuel-supply methane scaled to the inventory of the last inventory year (k, from the stored scenario-1 values); energy N2O follows energy CO2; industrial processes follow industrial energy CO2 (IndustrialProcessEmissionsScaleEner); agriculture, waste and other follow income and population with the non-energy elasticities (\(m\): the ratio of CO2 to the baseline when AdditionMitigationPoliciesNonEnergy); agriculture and waste CH4 come from the methane block (A7.3); LULUCF CO2 declines by LULUCFAnnualEmissionsDecline of the inventory value while positive. Totals exclude LULUCF; ghg.inc includes it. Kaya rows (section 13) index population, GDP per capita, energy and carbon intensity to the base year. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation sections 13 (Kaya) and 14.
A7.3 Methane by source and the methane fee (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ch4.abt}_s, \ \mathtt{ch4.act}_s, \ \mathtt{ch4.int}_s, \ \mathtt{ch4.em}_s, \ \mathtt{ch4.prd}_f = \mathtt{ch4.prd}_{f,t-1}\,\mathtt{ch4.pi}_f^{\epsilon_f}\,\frac{WD_{f,t-1}}{WD_{f,t-2}}, \ \mathtt{ch4.rev}, \ \mathtt{ch4.revf}
\]
Over sources \(s\) (oil and gas, downstream gas, coal mining, biomass, livestock, rice, waste), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 14). Abatement curve \(A, B\) by source (CH4Inputs); \(\iota_s\) whether the fee applies; activity: oil and gas and coal production (from the base year plus one, with world demand and the price response to the fee cost passed through), gas and biomass use, and income and population drivers for livestock, rice and waste; base emissions \(M_{s,0}\) are the inventory CH4 of the last inventory year split by source shares (fuel sources capped by MethShareCap relative to activity). ch4.revf is the fee revenue with gas and biomass use of the stored baseline. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 14 (ch4.*).
A7.4 NDC target and gap (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ndc.lvl}, \ \mathtt{ndc.r}, \ \mathtt{ndc.red}, \ \mathtt{ndc.gap}, \ \mathtt{ndc.over} = \mathtt{ghg.inc} - \mathtt{ndc.lvl}_{sel}
\]
Over years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 14, NDC rows; computed after the year loop because they read the baseline at the target year \(ty\)). The NDC row (Latest, or the first or second round) gives the type (BAU, fixed, historical, intensity, unquantifiable), target years, reference year, unconditional and conditional changes, LULUCF and gas coverage; the level \(\ell\) by type; the reduction selected by Conditionality (average of the two where not chosen). Text rows and ‘N/A’ are not compared numerically. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 14 (ndc.).
A7.5 Carbon pricing indicators (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{tcp}_f, \ \mathtt{cov.ct}_S, \ \mathtt{cov.ets}, \ \mathtt{cov.all}, \ \mathtt{cpeff} = \mathtt{cptraj}\cdot\mathtt{cov.ct}, \ \mathtt{ecr}
\]
Over fuels \(f\), sector groups \(S\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 17). Revenue by fuel includes the power fuel rows (coal, gas, oil); covered CO2 (covct, A6.2) and ETS-covered CO2 as shares of energy CO2. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 17.
A7.6 Local air pollutants (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{ap}_{s,p}, \ \mathtt{ap.w}, \ \mathtt{apfd}, \ \mathtt{apf}_p, \ \mathtt{aps}_{src,p}, \ \mathtt{apen}, \ \mathtt{ghg.enrp} = \mathtt{ghg}_{enr,all} + \mathtt{apf}_{all}
\]
Over pollutants \(p\) (PM2.5, NOx, SO2, VOC, BC, OC, CO), subsectors \(s\) and power, sources (coal and gas plants, other power, road, ground level, other, food and agriculture). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 15, read by the air pollution module). Combustion factors of the base year and the final year (A7.1), weighted by \(w_t\) (EFSel share \(\omega\), final year EFEndYear); power by generation type. Food processing uses the food share of the energy balance; agriculture is the rest of food and forestry. By source, POM = 1.3 OC and other PM = PM2.5 - BC - POM (at least 0); methane by source from the CH4 rows. GWP100 of the GAINS region of the country. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 15.


B.3.8 A8 GDP and results
GDP multipliers, external balance, the inputs of the modules (section 17b), welfare, subsidies and efficient prices (section 18).
A8.1 Fiscal multipliers by lag (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{fis.grp} = \text{global | est | man by MultipliersSource, else the income group}, \quad \mathtt{fis.key} = g|\text{FmAdj}|, \quad s = 0, -1, +1 \ (\text{base, low, high})
\]
Over instruments \(i\) (exc, pit, cit, vat, capt, gnfs, trns, wage), lags \(k\). Excel-AI notation (Inputs rows 456-486): MFMOD median and standard deviation by income group (or global); lags past the last data lag (11) hold its value. Country-estimated and manual multipliers (Est, Man) are not in Coded CPAT yet. Source: Excel-AI: Inputs rows 454-486.
A8.2 External balance (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{xnim}_{all,f}, \ \mathtt{xnim}_{grp,g}, \ \mathtt{xtb}_{all,g}, \ \mathtt{xtbp} = \mathtt{xtb} - \mathtt{xnim}, \ \mathtt{bca.r} = \mathtt{bca}\cdot\mathtt{infl}, \ \mathtt{bca.p}, \ \mathtt{bca.pp} = \mathtt{bca.gdp} + \textstyle\sum_g \mathtt{bca.d}_g / \mathtt{bca.y}
\]
Over fuels \(f\), trade groups \(g\) (oil products, gas, coal), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 16b; Inputs_macro trade rows, legacy rows 741-743). Base-year imports \(M\), production \(P\), exports \(X\) (negative) from the energy balance; the change in use against the baseline (echg) at the supply price; the trade balance at the real international price of scenario 1’s source (GJ per barrel, MMBtu, tonne). The current account is WEO’s (USD bn and % of GDP), held after the last data year; bca.n (current prices) is 0 after it (issue I130). Excel-AI types Egypt’s WEO values; Coded CPAT reads WEO for any country. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 16b; Inputs_macro.
A8.3 Air pollution costs and PM2.5 concentration from the module (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{airpol.cost}_c, \ \mathtt{airpol.cost.gj}_c, \ \mathtt{fus}_{s,f} = \mathtt{ener}_{s,f}, \ \mathtt{fuq}_{S,f}, \ \mathtt{air.con.pm2}_{src}
\]
Over price codes \(c\), sector groups \(S\), sources (coal, gas and other power plants, road, ground level, other, food), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 17b). As A1.2 but weighted by the current year’s fuel use (the plain average where it is 0); per unit for oil products, per GJ in airpol.cost.gj; residential coal only above ApCoalResMin of buildings use. The concentration coefficients \(\kappa\) are the module’s (typed FromAirPollution). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 17b.
A8.4 Transport externalities per unit of road fuel (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{tran.}k\mathtt{.cost}_f = \mathtt{tran.}k\mathtt{.km}\cdot\mathtt{traf}_f\cdot\mathtt{tran.mrg}_f\cdot\mathtt{tran.rsh}_f\,(\cdot\,\mathtt{tran.fsh}_f), \quad \mathtt{tran.wcl}_f = 1 - \frac{\mathtt{trfcf}^{B}_f}{\mathtt{tran.cls}^{B}_f}, \quad \mathtt{tran.}k\mathtt{.gj} = \mathtt{tran.}k\mathtt{.cost} / gj
\]
Over kinds \(k\) (accidents, congestion, road damage), road fuels \(f\) (gasoline, diesel, LPG, gas, electricity), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 17b, rows 8510-8556). The cost per vehicle-km of the transport co-benefits module times the average fuel economy of the road engineer model (km per liter or kWh), the marginal share of distance in a change of fuel use (\(w_f\): the passenger share of the fuel’s use in the baseline; gasoline 1), the road share of the fuel; road damage only for the freight share \(\phi_f\). Per GJ for gasoline, diesel and LPG (A8.5). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 17b.
A8.5 Welfare gains (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{wel.all.usd} = \mathtt{wcli.all.nat} + \mathtt{wel.air.usd} + \textstyle\sum \mathtt{wel.rod.*.usd} - \mathtt{eff.tot.tot} - \mathtt{mfc.tot.tot}, \quad \mathtt{eff}_f = -\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathtt{wdg}_f + \mathtt{wdg}^{B}_f)\,\mathtt{echg}_f / 1000, \quad \mathtt{wdg}_f = \frac{\mathtt{rfu}_f + \mathtt{rfg.pow}_f}{\mathtt{ener}_f}
\]
Over fuels \(f\), methane sources, years \(t\); in USD bn and in % of GDP (wel.*.pct). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 18, rows 8566-8671, 9063). Climate at the national social cost of carbon; air pollution at the value of PM2.5 concentration (module); road transport at the module’s cost per km of the change in distance (road engineer model); the efficiency cost at the average fuel tax per ktoe of the scenario and the baseline (methodology: \(ddw = \tfrac{1}{2}(nc - xcp)(F_P - F_B)\)); the abatement cost of the methane fee (marginal price capped at the source’s full abatement, times \(b/(1+b)\) of the abatement). Also the environmental gain of the change in fossil fuel use at the global climate cost plus the air pollution and transport costs per GJ (env.ffs.cost, wel.ffs). Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 18.
A8.6 Fossil fuel subsidies and efficient prices (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{expsub.con}_i, \ \mathtt{impsub.con}_i, \ \mathtt{effprice} = \mathtt{supcost} + \mathtt{extcost} + \mathtt{vatext}; \quad \mathtt{eff.price}_c = \mathtt{sup.cost}_c + \mathtt{pig}_c + \mathtt{vat.cost}_c, \ \mathtt{tgap}_c = \mathtt{rp.eff}_c - \mathtt{eff.price}_c, \ \mathtt{pig.co2e}_c = \mathtt{pig}_c\,\frac{SCC^{glo}}{\mathtt{scc.cost}_c}
\]
Over price rows \(i\) (oil products; gas, coal and electricity by industry, residential, power and other: the use-weighted average), price codes \(c\), years \(t\). Excel-AI notation (Mitigation section 18, rows 8675-9059). Subsidies: supply cost of the year, external cost (global climate, air pollution, road transport per GJ), VAT at the general rate (VAT_WEO of 2022, Excel-AI VatGen) on both where consumers pay VAT (oil products times the household share); use in PJ (GWh). Efficient prices per price unit: the baseline supply cost, the Pigouvian taxes (air pollution, climate cost of the price code, road transport), VAT on the supply cost and, where ExternalityAddVAT, on the Pigouvian taxes; the averages weighted by use. Source: Excel-AI: Mitigation section 18.

text:
B.4 Adjustments: distribution
Excel-AI Distribution 0.1.3 (methodology chapter 5).

B.4.1 B1 Distribution
B1.1 Input-output data of the country (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{gtot}_k = \mathtt{DIOTot}_k, \qquad \mathtt{DLcat}_{g,k} = \frac{\sum_{i \in g} \mathtt{HHD}_i\,L_{i,k}}{\sum_{i \in g} \mathtt{HHD}_i}
\]
Over fuel groups \(k\), GTAP sectors \(i\), categories \(g\). Total use of fuel group \(k\): embedded in the total demand \(TD\) and exports \(X\) of non-fuel sectors plus its own demand, at ResultsYear prices (WEO GDP deflator \(D\) over the GTAP year). Source: Excel-AI: DistMapping.
B1.2 Survey to national accounts (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{pop\_tot\_adj} = \mathtt{popw}\cdot\mathtt{popadj}, \quad \mathtt{cons\_pc\_na} = \mathtt{cons\_pc\_svy}\cdot\mathtt{consadj}, \quad \mathtt{tot\_cons\_na} = \mathtt{cons\_pc\_na}\cdot\mathtt{pop\_tot\_adj}, \quad \mathtt{nacons} = \mathtt{gdp}\cdot\mathtt{consgdp}/100
\]
Over deciles, samples. Population and GDP (local currency) of the scenario in YearDistn; private consumption in % of GDP from WDI (NE.CON.PRVT.ZS) in its latest year. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_4, eq-5_5; Excel-AI: Distribution section 7.
B1.3 Mitigation-adjusted incidence and deadweight loss (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{badj} = \min(1, \max(0, \mathtt{rev}/\mathtt{revimpl})), \quad \mathtt{revimpl} = \textstyle\sum_d \mathtt{uloss}_d\,\mathtt{tot\_cons\_na}_d / 100, \quad \mathtt{lscale} = \mathtt{badj} + \mathtt{DWLTri}\,(1 - \mathtt{badj})
\]
With InferredDist = Yes the burden is scaled to the revenue mitigation actually raises (\(\beta\) = 1 otherwise); with DWLs = Yes the deadweight triangle is added. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_6; Excel-AI: Distribution section 6.
B1.4 Cooking-fuel exemption (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{fac}_{f,d} = 0 \text{ where } \mathtt{exdec}_d = 1 \text{ and } f = \mathtt{exfuel}
\]
Over deciles \(d \le\) ExemptCookDeciles. The main cooking fuel of the country (WHO) when ExemptMostCook = Yes. Source: Excel-AI: Distribution sections 1 and 4.
B1.5 Personal income tax cut (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{pit} = \mathtt{pitpa} \mid \mathtt{pitprop} \mid \mathtt{pitte} \ (\mathtt{PITReductionType}), \quad \mathtt{pitbase} = \mathtt{gdp}\cdot\mathtt{pitind}/100
\]
Over deciles \(d\). Personal allowance, proportional compensation or targeted exemption from the bottom up to decile DistExcCfDec (\(P_{d-1}\) the PIT paid by the deciles below). PIT shares \(s_d\) by MissingDataReplacement. Source: Excel-AI: Distribution section 8.
B1.6 Public investment and current spending (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{pui}_d = \mathtt{puiamt}\,\mathtt{noacc}_d, \quad \mathtt{noacc} = 1 - \mathtt{acs}/100, \qquad \mathtt{cts}_d = \mathtt{ctsamt}\,\mathtt{aspbase}_d
\]
Over deciles \(d\), samples (public investment). \(a_d\) access to the infrastructure chosen (PublicInfrastructureInvType); \(b_d\) the ASPIRE benefit of the programme chosen (CurrentSpendingType) by quintile. Source: methodology: 05_Distribution, eq-5_13, eq-5_14; Excel-AI: Distribution section 8.
B1.7 Gini coefficient (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{gini.g0}, \ \mathtt{gini.gx}, \ \mathtt{gini.gi} \text{ of } \mathtt{tot\_cons\_na}, \ \mathtt{postx}, \ \mathtt{posti}, \quad \mathtt{pct\_gini\_rec} = (\mathtt{gini.gi}/\mathtt{gini.g0} - 1)\cdot 100
\]
Over samples. The legacy Gini: a quadratic Lorenz curve through the origin fitted to the ten decile points (least squares), linear in the decile totals \(x_d\) (weights \(W_d\), DistMapping DGiniW). Before (postx) and after (posti) recycling. Source: Excel-AI: Distribution section 9; DistMapping DGiniW.
B1.8 Price change by production sector (adjustment)
\[
\mathtt{dps}_i, \ \mathtt{dpsp}_i = \mathtt{dps}_i\cdot\mathtt{passthrough}_{s(i)}, \ \mathtt{dprk}_i, \ \mathtt{ppic}_s, \ \mathtt{ppici}_s, \ \mathtt{outpriin}_s
\]
Over GTAP sectors \(i\), CPAT sectors \(s\) (by output \(Q\) or household demand). Pass-through \(\gamma\) where PassthroughDist = Yes; the 20 sectors with the largest price change listed (ties by sheet order). Source: Excel-AI: Distribution section 11.
